edges.description: Loss of an alpha-tubulin isotype impairs assembly of the microtubule spindle.
Faulty spindles are expected to disturb chromosome segregation in the oocyte or early embryo, but which division fails and how this produces arrest before the blastocyst stage has not been shown.
Arrested embryos cannot be transferred to establish a pregnancy.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense (p.Gln358Ter) and frameshift (p.Asp444Metfs*42) variants truncate or alter the C-terminal part of tubulin alpha-1C. TUBA1C is an alpha-tubulin isotype expressed during oogenesis and early embryogenesis, where it contributes to the microtubule network alongside other tubulins such as TUBB8. The variants are treated as loss of function; whether p.Gln358Ter transcripts undergo nonsense-mediated decay is not stated in the abstract.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic variants in α-tubulin isotypes cause female infertility characterised as recurrent preimplantation embryo arrest.
evidence.snippet: Four homozygous variants were identified in the PREA cohort: two of TUBA1C (p.Gln358Ter and p.Asp444Metfs*42) and two of TUBA4A (p.Arg339Cys and p.Tyr440Ter).

genetic_context.description: One nonsense and one frameshift variant, each homozygous in one proband.

nodes.description: The TUBA1C variants (together with the TUBA4A variants reported alongside them) cause spindle assembly defects of varying severity in in vitro functional assays. The abstract does not say whether the assays were done in oocytes, embryos, or cultured cells, so the node is not restricted to meiotic or mitotic spindles, and no spindle phenotype has been examined in patient oocytes or embryos. No cell type is bound for the same reason.

nodes.description: Embryos from affected women repeatedly arrest before the blastocyst stage (recurrent preimplantation embryo arrest), the defining presentation of the cohort in which the variants were found. The arrest stage is not reported in the abstract.
